newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS CATTLE TRADE MODERATE AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS CATTLE TRADE MODERATE AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle Friday traded at $64.00 in moderate volume, down $1.00 from earlier in the week, but off $2.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said. About 5,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area and about 1,000 in Kansas.

Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by a precipitous drop in beef prices, with the heavyweight choice closing values quoted $103.21 per cwt, down $5.66 since last Friday's close, USDA statistics show.
Sales this week were light as owners reluctantly sold cattle at $64, representing a loss of about $20.00 a head.

Many feedlots reportedly were fairly current coming into this week so they could handle carrying over cattle, market sources said. However, the extra cattle next week could stymie attempts to sell cattle at higher prices.
Packer bids on Monday were seen at $62.00 to $63.00, with most owners expected to price cattle at $65.00 to $66.00.

Owners were seen optimisitic on ideas this week's lower beef prices could invite stronger retail demand for promotions for the Labor Day holiday, September 1, several sources said. The Labor Day weekend marks the unofficial end to summer and the outdoor cooking season.
